name: quotient_filter
description: Aggregate that builds a Quotient filter from hashed keys. `q` controls slot count (2^q slots), `r` controls remainder bits per slot. Quotient filters support deletion and resize — use them when the underlying set evolves over time.

examples.description: Build a Quotient filter per partition
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE filters AS
SELECT id % 2 AS remainder,
       quotient_filter(16, 4, hash(id)) AS filter
FROM series_data
GROUP BY id % 2;

name: quotient_filter_contains
description: Test whether a hash value is a member of a Quotient filter. Returns BOOLEAN — false means definitely-not-present; true means probably-present (within the filter's configured false-positive rate).

examples.description: Membership test against a stored filter
examples.code:
SELECT quotient_filter_contains(filter, hash(12345)) AS might_exist
FROM filters WHERE remainder = 1;

name: xor8_filter
description: Aggregate that builds an 8-bit XOR filter from hashed keys. ~9 bits per key, ~0.39% false positive rate. Static — built once, queried many times. ~20% smaller than Bloom for the same FPR.

examples.description: Build an xor8 filter from a column of hashed IDs
examples.code: SELECT xor8_filter(hash(id)) AS filter FROM ids;

name: xor16_filter
description: Aggregate that builds a 16-bit XOR filter from hashed keys. ~18 bits per key, ~0.0015% false positive rate. Use when you need a much lower FPR than xor8 and can afford 2× the memory.

examples.description: Build an xor16 filter for low FPR
examples.code: SELECT xor16_filter(hash(id)) AS filter FROM ids;

name: xor8_filter_contains
description: Test whether a hash value is a member of an 8-bit XOR filter.

name: xor16_filter_contains
description: Test whether a hash value is a member of a 16-bit XOR filter.

name: binary_fuse8_filter
description: Aggregate that builds an 8-bit Binary Fuse filter from hashed keys. The most space-efficient filter family — typically <9 bits per key — with very fast construction and lookups. Static structure.

examples.code: SELECT binary_fuse8_filter(hash(id)) AS filter FROM ids;

name: binary_fuse16_filter
description: Aggregate that builds a 16-bit Binary Fuse filter — same family as binary_fuse8 but with much lower false-positive rate at the cost of ~2× the memory.

examples.code: SELECT binary_fuse16_filter(hash(id)) AS filter FROM ids;

name: binary_fuse8_filter_contains
description: Test whether a hash value is a member of an 8-bit Binary Fuse filter.

name: binary_fuse16_filter_contains
description: Test whether a hash value is a member of a 16-bit Binary Fuse filter.

name: bitfilters_duckdb_bloom_filter_create
description: Build a Bloom filter compatible with DuckDB's internal join filter format. Produced filters can be used in custom join optimization paths and in zone-map-style data skipping.

name: bitfilters_duckdb_bloom_filter_probe
description: Test whether a hash value might be a member of a DuckDB-compatible Bloom filter built by `bitfilters_duckdb_bloom_filter_create`.

name: bitfilters_duckdb_hash
description: Hash function compatible with DuckDB's internal Bloom filter probe layout. Use this rather than a generic hash when feeding values into the DuckDB-style Bloom filter functions.
